title: Smart Apparel
desc: Understand and plan wearable-sensor clothing: materials, sensors, washing, data privacy and a small product pilot.
outcomes: Explain how sensors are built into fabric.
Plan a prototype for one use.
task: Plan and test a small smart-garment prototype (or a bought kit), with use case, materials list, washing test, data privacy plan and cost.
condition: Basic electronics kit or a purchased kit, fabric, a computer, two peers and a mentor. Safe low voltage only.
standard: Use case defined; washing test repeated and logged; accuracy compared to a reference; privacy plan written; low-voltage safety rules followed; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Fashion students, makers, sports teams, textile staff.
evidence: plan, test log, privacy plan, cost sheet
modules: Conductive threads, printed ink, small modules.
A shirt tracks breathing for athletes.
Silver yarn stays conductive after washing better than plain thread.
Choose sensor for the need; keep wires short.
Small battery with protection; low voltage.
A 3.7 V cell with a protection board.
Signals fail after 8 washes; sealing improves it.
The app stores data only on the phone.

Checked, dated and explained to others
local: Product-safety, textile labelling and health-data rules differ by place.
ladder: What smart apparel is

L1: learner can name uses. Focus module: What smart apparel is (Understand, 3 h). Clothing that senses. Key points: Heart rate, motion, temperature, posture. Conductive threads, printed ink, small modules. Use cases: sport, care, safety.

Teach: open with the worked example. A shirt tracks breathing for athletes. Then set the activity: List five use cases. Mark against the standard: Table. Check at this level: Name a use. Model answer: Sport, care or safety. Uses.
Materials

L2: learner knows materials. Focus module: Materials (Understand, 3 h). Comfort first. Key points: Stretch, breathable fabrics; skin-safe materials. Conductive yarn and flexible circuits. Allergy awareness.

Teach: open with the worked example. Silver yarn stays conductive after washing better than plain thread. Then set the activity: Compare materials. Mark against the standard: Table. Check at this level: Why removable module? Model answer: For washing. Materials.
Sensors and power

L3: learner can design a block. Focus module: Sensors and power (Apply, 4 h). Make it work. Key points: Choose sensor for the need; keep wires short. Small battery with protection; low voltage. Waterproof modules.

Teach: open with the worked example. A 3.7 V cell with a protection board. Then set the activity: Design a block diagram. Mark against the standard: Parts labelled. Check at this level: Safe voltage? Model answer: Low voltage. Design.
Prototype
L4: learner can build. Focus module: Prototype (Apply, 4 h). Build small. Key points: Sew or attach; strain relief. Test continuity and signal. Keep modules removable for washing.

Teach: open with the worked example. A removable module cuts failures. Then set the activity: Build or plan a prototype. Mark against the standard: Test passes. Check at this level: Accuracy measure? Model answer: Percent error. Build.
Wash and wear tests
L5: learner can test. Focus module: Wash and wear tests (Analyse, 4 h). Real use. Key points: Wash cycles; sweat; stretch. Count cycles until failure. Comfort rating by users.

Teach: open with the worked example. Signals fail after 8 washes; sealing improves it. Then set the activity: Run tests. Mark against the standard: Log complete. Check at this level: Material concern? Model answer: Skin allergy. Test.
Privacy, safety and rules

L6: learner can lead a pilot. Focus module: Privacy, safety and rules (Evaluate, 4 h). Health data matters. Key points: Consent; secure storage; clear purpose. Battery and skin safety. Claims must be modest.

Teach: open with the worked example. The app stores data only on the phone. Then set the activity: Write a plan. Mark against the standard: Items listed. Check at this level: Privacy rule? Model answer: Consent and secure storage. Lead.
Cost and pilot
L7: learner can audit. Focus module: Cost and pilot (Create, 3 h). Small first run. Key points: Cost per garment; price. Pilot with 10 users. Feedback and repair plan.

Teach: open with the worked example. Cost 780 INR; price 1,600 INR. Then set the activity: Cost and plan. Mark against the standard: Currency shown. Check at this level: Wash test? Model answer: Count cycles to failure. Peer audit.
